advisory.finding: The three-branch nested ternary selecting how to call _referencing_commits is functionally equivalent to a single unconditional call. _referencing_commits defaults metrics=None and ticket_view=None and treats them as omitted (line 371, 378), so passing metrics=None / ticket_view=None is indistinguishable from not passing them. The branching adds no behavior and obscures the call.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide and document whether the post-refresh rescan should record its own metric keys (or accumulate) rather than silently overwriting the first scan's metrics at close_precheck.py:217.
advisory.finding: When the remote is present and the refresh succeeds, the post-fetch rescan passes metrics=metrics, so its writes to metrics (git_history_read_ms, referencing_commits_found, alias_index_build_ms, etc.) silently overwrite the values recorded by the first HEAD-only scan. Downstream metric consumers will see only the second scan's numbers, not an aggregate or the original view.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm behavior (and add coverage) for a detached-HEAD refreshed clone where upstream_branch_refs is empty; ensure the post-refresh rescan does not silently misreport a merged commit as absent.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine_support/commit_impact.py:171: Empty on a detached HEAD, in a
advisory.finding: On a detached-HEAD checkout, upstream_branch_refs returns [] (it requires `git symbolic-ref --short HEAD`), so the post-fetch rescan with include_upstream=True degrades to HEAD-only and cannot see commits the fetch pulled onto refs/remotes/*. In that case the gate still raises the ordinary 'no commit references it' refusal even though the fetch obtained the referencing commit — the exact misleading refusal the ticket set out to eliminate.
